title: 442. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Period of a Sine or Cosine Graph
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Find the period of a sine function whose argument is multiplied by a constant.
questions.question: What is the period of \(y=\sin 2x\)?
questions.explanation: The period of \(y=\sin(Bx)\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{|B|}\). With \(B=2\), the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi\). The graph completes its cycle twice as fast, so the period is halved, not doubled.

questions.learningObjective: Find the period of a cosine function whose argument is divided by a constant.
questions.question: What is the period of \(y=\cos\frac{x}{3}\)?
questions.explanation: Here \(B=\frac{1}{3}\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{1/3}=6\pi\). Dividing \(x\) by \(3\) stretches the graph horizontally, making the period three times as long. The value \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) is the period of \(y=\cos 3x\).
questions.hint: Write the argument as \(Bx\) with \(B=\frac{1}{3}\), then compute \(\frac{2\pi}{B}\).

questions.concept: Period with pi in the argument
questions.learningObjective: Find the period when the coefficient of the variable is pi.
questions.question: What is the period of \(y=4\sin(\pi x)\)?
questions.explanation: Here \(B=\pi\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{\pi}=2\). The factor \(4\) is the amplitude and does not affect the period. Multiplying \(2\pi\) by \(\pi\) instead of dividing gives the incorrect \(2\pi^2\).
questions.hint: Divide \(2\pi\) by the coefficient of \(x\); the factors of \(\pi\) cancel.

questions.concept: Period with a vertical shift present
questions.learningObjective: Find the period of a cosine function that also has a vertical shift.
questions.question: What is the period of \(y=\cos(3x)+5\)?
questions.explanation: The period depends only on the coefficient of \(x\): \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\). The added constant \(5\) moves the graph up without changing how often it repeats. The value \(6\pi\) would be the period of \(y=\cos\frac{x}{3}\).
questions.hint: Only the coefficient of \(x\) affects the period.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the coefficient of the variable that produces a given period.
questions.question: For which positive value of \(B\) does \(y=\sin(Bx)\) have period \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Then \(B=2\pi\cdot\frac{2}{\pi}=4\). With \(B=\frac{1}{4}\) the period would be \(8\pi\), far longer than required.

questions.learningObjective: Recognise that the amplitude and a reflection do not affect the period.
questions.question: What is the period of \(y=-2\sin(5x)\)?
questions.explanation: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|B|}=\frac{2\pi}{5}\). The factor \(-2\) changes the amplitude to \(2\) and reflects the graph, but the graph still repeats every \(\frac{2\pi}{5}\). Multiplying the period by the amplitude gives the incorrect \(\frac{4\pi}{5}\).
questions.hint: Decide which number in the rule controls horizontal stretching.

questions.concept: Number of cycles in an interval
questions.learningObjective: Count the complete cycles of a sine graph on a given interval.
questions.question: How many complete cycles does the graph of \(y=\sin 4x\) make for \(0\le x\le 2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}\). The interval has length \(2\pi\), so the number of cycles is \(2\pi\div\frac{\pi}{2}=4\). In general, \(y=\sin(Bx)\) completes \(B\) cycles on an interval of length \(2\pi\).
questions.hint: Divide the length of the interval by the period.

questions.learningObjective: Find the period of a sine function when the variable is measured in degrees.
questions.question: The variable \(x\) is measured in degrees. What is the period of \(y=\sin(6x)\)?
questions.explanation: In degrees, one full cycle of the sine requires the argument to increase by \(360^\circ\). So \(6x\) must increase by \(360^\circ\), which means \(x\) increases by \(\frac{360^\circ}{6}=60^\circ\). Multiplying \(360^\circ\) by \(6\) gives the incorrect \(2160^\circ\).
questions.hint: In degree measure, replace \(2\pi\) by \(360^\circ\) in the period formula.

questions.learningObjective: Use the absolute value of the coefficient when computing a period.
questions.question: What is the period of \(y=\cos\left(-\frac{2x}{3}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|B|}\) with \(B=-\frac{2}{3}\): \(\frac{2\pi}{2/3}=3\pi\). A period is a positive length, so the absolute value of the coefficient is used. Since cosine is even, the function equals \(\cos\frac{2x}{3}\) anyway.
questions.hint: A period is a positive number; use the absolute value of the coefficient of \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the period and coefficient from the positions of consecutive maximum points.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\cos\left(B(x-1)\right)\) with \(B>0\) has consecutive maximum points at \(x=1\) and \(x=7\). What is \(B\)?
questions.explanation: Consecutive maxima are one period apart, so the period is \(7-1=6\). Then \(\frac{2\pi}{B}=6\) gives \(B=\frac{\pi}{3}\). The value \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) would give period \(12\), which would be correct only if the distance \(6\) were half a period.
questions.hint: The distance between consecutive maxima is one full period.
